title: 10 · Quillon on a laptop and a phone
strengths: One product on two screens, and the data agrees to the cent: vendor, amount, budget, policy, the four-step chain and the times match between laptop and phone
The light is one scene: one softbox from the upper left, soft shadows falling right with dark contact lines; nothing is pasted
Neither device copies a brand's outline, and the screens read at 100%: the phone's amounts and chain, the laptop's title, amount and both buttons
slop_signals: The laptop reads as a 3D model, not a product: a thick flat slab with a rounded rim, keys in a black well, a flat grey trackpad, and a barrel hinge that sits on top of the deck and covers half of the function-key row
The keyboard has both an 'opt' and an 'alt' key on the bottom row ('fn ctrl opt alt'), which no real layout has
Platform mismatch: the phone runs an iOS screen (left clock, '< Approvals' back label, iOS tab bar) on Android-style hardware with a centred punch-hole and side keys
Composition: the top fifth of the frame is empty set, and the devices sit low and small; shipped multi-device sections fill the frame or show the screens flat
No shipped B2B reference found uses a chunky path-traced laptop; they use flat frontal device outlines or no device
fixes: Replace the 3D laptop with a flat, frontal, generic frame (as Riverside does) or show the web screen flat with the phone overlapping its corner (as Wispr Flow does); if the render stays, thin the base, move the hinge behind the keyboard and use one real layout ('fn ctrl alt' or 'fn control option command')
Make the phone hardware match its iOS screen without copying Apple: no visible camera cut-out at all, or a plain rounded slab
Crop or reframe so the devices fill about 85% of the width and the empty set above them goes
Fix the 'Waiting on others · 6' count (the list holds 5) or add the sixth row

references.what: Tablet, laptop and phone as flat, frontal, generic frames filling the width; the screens carry everything
